mainEntity.name: How much does a Jaguar XKR-S engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt Jaguar XKR-S engine typically costs between £5,900 and £8,500 for supply only, depending on whether it is the 4.2L (AJ34S) or 5.0L (AJ133) variant. Supply and fit packages generally add £1,500-£2,200 for specialist labour, supercharger servicing, and mandatory JLR diagnostic coding.

mainEntity.name: What are the common signs my Jaguar XKR-S engine is failing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Rattle on startup points to timing chain tensioner failure. A distinct rattling noise from the front of the engine that changes with revs suggests supercharger coupler wear. Sudden loss of oil pressure or a knocking sound means bottom end bearing failure or oil pump drive failure - stop driving immediately.

mainEntity.name: Is the 4.2L or 5.0L XKR-S engine more reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both share similar vulnerabilities regarding supercharger coupler wear and timing chain tensioner degradation. However, the 5.0L Gen III (AJ133) carries the additional risk of oil pump drive failure (Recall JAG-19V-005). Neither is inherently "unreliable" if preventative maintenance is strictly followed, but the 5.0L requires more vigilant monitoring of its oil pump and cooling systems.

mainEntity.name: Does a replacement Jaguar XKR-S engine need ECU coding?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, this is non-negotiable. All AJ-V8 engines require JLR SDD or Pathfinder diagnostic tool programming to synchronise the immobiliser, recognise the new engine's parameters, and calibrate the supercharger and VVT systems. Specialist fitting services always include this.

mainEntity.name: Can I fit a 5.0L XKR-S engine into my standard 4.2L XKR or XK?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not a direct swap. You would need the XKR-S ECU, complete engine harness, upgraded cooling system (including intercooler pumps), transmission modifications, and different engine mounts and differential. It is prohibitively expensive and complex.

historyTimeline.h2: Jaguar XKR-S - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the Jaguar XKR-S launched, it served as the limited-run, track-focused pinnacle of the X150 generation, featuring significantly upgraded cooling, suspension, and supercharger components over the standard XKR to handle extreme performance demands.

milestones.description: XKR-S 4.2 introduced. AJ34S 4.2L supercharged V8, 420hp. Limited production run (e.g., 200 UK coupes) with identical power output to the standard XKR but distinct aerodynamic and chassis tuning.
XKR-S 5.0 launched. AJ133 5.0L supercharged Gen III V8, 550hp. Featured revised ECU mapping, upgraded supercharger cooling, and a significant power increase over the previous generation.
XKR-S GT 5.0 introduced as the ultimate, ultra-limited variant, retaining the 550hp AJ133 engine but with further track-focused aerodynamic and chassis refinements.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Jaguar XKR-S is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points specific to these high-performance variants.

commonProblems.h2: Jaguar XKR-S Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Jaguar XKR-S reliability profile is heavily influenced by the inherent stresses of its supercharged AJ-V8 architecture. Supercharger coupler degradation, timing chain tensioner wear, and (on the 5.0L) oil pump drive failure are the most frequently reported issues. Every rebuilt Jaguar XKR-S engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded internal components specifically designed to address these original factory failure points, backed by a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Supercharger Coupler Failure - Why the Jaguar XKR-S Loses Boost
problems.rootCause: The Eaton supercharger uses a nylon/plastic coupler between the snout shaft and rotor pack. Heat cycling and torsional stress cause the coupler to wear down, creating a rattle at idle and progressive boost loss.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt engine including fully serviced supercharger with upgraded coupler, new timing components, bench tested
repairOptions.longevity: 100k+ miles. The only option if coupler failure caused debris ingestion or secondary engine damage.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Jaguar XKR-S of relevant age is worth £15,000-£45,000+. In this value band, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine at £5,900-£8,500 usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability, protecting the vehicle's significant residual value.
problems.recommendation: Replace the coupler the moment you hear rattling from the front of the supercharger. At specialist prices (£800-£1,200), it is preventative maintenance that protects a £2,000+ supercharger. If you have already lost boost or hear grinding, opt for the full supercharger rebuild. XKR-S owners who ignore the rattle often face engine replacement when coupler debris circulates.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for XKR-S supercharged engine replacement with upgraded couplers

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Failure - Why the Jaguar XKR-S AJ-V8 Fails Prematurely
problems.rootCause: Plastic timing chain tensioner shoes become brittle with heat cycles and oil contamination, then crack or shatter. Chain slack follows, skipping teeth on cam sprockets, leading to valve-to-piston contact.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full timing chain set replacement with upgraded steel-caged tensioners, new guides, cam sprockets, and crankshaft bolt
repairOptions.longevity: 80k-100k miles. Only viable if engine has NO rattling or fault codes. Prevents catastrophic failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Timing components + cylinder head removal, valve inspection, camshaft replacement if damaged
repairOptions.longevity: Unknown - hidden bottom end damage may surface later. Often a gamble vs full replacement.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt engine with upgraded timing components, new gaskets, oil pump, bench tested before dispatch
repairOptions.longevity: 100k+ miles expected. Includes 12-month unlimited mileage warranty. All known weak points addressed.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a Jaguar XKR-S valued between £15,000 and £45,000, investing in a rebuilt engine is financially sound if catastrophic timing failure has occurred, as it restores reliability without the steep depreciation hit of scrapping the vehicle.
problems.recommendation: If you catch the rattle early and have no fault codes, preventative replacement at a specialist (£1,800-£2,800) is excellent value. Once the chain has slipped, we recommend going straight to a rebuilt engine. The labour overlap is significant, and the repaired engine still carries risk of hidden bottom end damage.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt AJ-V8 engine prices for your Jaguar XKR-S

problems.h4: Oil Pump Drive Failure - Recall JAG-19V-005 Explained (5.0L Specific)
problems.rootCause: The oil pump drive sleeve (connecting the crankshaft to the pump rotor) fractures due to inadequate material strength and harmonics. Oil pressure drops to zero without warning. The engine seizes within minutes.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of oil pump assembly with revised JAG-19V-005 spec unit, new drive sleeve, sump gasket, oil and filter
repairOptions.longevity: Permanent fix with revised component. Only viable if engine has NO oil pressure warning and NO knocking.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt engine with revised oil pump drive, new timing components, fully tested
repairOptions.longevity: 100k+ miles. The only reliable option if the engine has seized or thrown a rod. 12-month warranty included.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Given the high value of the XKR-S 5.0, the £900-£1,400 preventative oil pump replacement is the cheapest insurance you can buy. Once the pump fails and the engine seizes, replacement is your only reliable path.
problems.recommendation: If your 5.0L XKR-S has no record of Recall JAG-19V-005 being performed, spend the £900-£1,400 on preventative oil pump replacement at a specialist. Once the pump fails and the engine seizes, replacement is your only reliable path. The post-failure repair cost approaches replacement cost with an inferior outcome.
